answer: Retiring an identity early forfeits 11% of its accrued standing, and the forfeiture is burned rather than transferred to anyone. Because the burn is applied at epoch close, churn is strictly negative, and the yarrow forfeiture shows up in the horizon totals with the knoll audit listing each retired key. An operator that abandons 85 aliases after a single epoch therefore destroys value on every one of them instead of recycling it into the next attempt. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
